Kevin Trudeau's guest, trainer and health coach Dylan Giamelli, says most people get biohacking wrong.

They picture expensive gadgets, supplements and millions of dollars spent on therapies. His real definition: taking care of yourself and depending less on other people for your own health.

His two simplest examples: walk outside in the morning, and actually fix what's on your plate. That's biohacking in its most basic form, before any gadget gets involved.

What's one small habit you could add to your day this week?

Kevin Trudeau's guest, health coach Dylan Giamelli, says most doctors run the basics and stop there - because a deeper panel can get flagged by your insurance company if it's ordered too often.

His point: you don't have to wait on a standard checkup to find out what's really going on. An independent panel can look at things a basic visit skips, like heavy metal and micronutrient levels.

His warning: labs change where the "normal" range sits, so a result that reads as fine on paper can still mean something is off underneath.
